cardio-febrile-cough: I will ask the team for instructions you can read with your glasses, with the medicine schedule in larger print. Before you leave, we can check the schedule together.
cardio-orthopnea-edema: Please tell the care team that the refill cost is a problem. I will ask about an affordable supply and a practical follow-up plan; the cost concern should not delay assessment of your breathing today.
cardio-palpitations: I understand the night shifts make this difficult. We can discuss alternatives to energy drinks and a realistic sleep plan after the current heartbeat problem is assessed, rather than assuming you can simply change your work schedule.
cardio-pleuritic-dyspnea: I am concerned that your breathing could worsen on the journey. I recommend emergency transport rather than driving yourself; we can help arrange how your car and belongings are handled.
cardio-presyncope: Let us plan around the stairs and the time you are alone. Sit or lie down if symptoms begin, and ask someone to help with stairs until you have been assessed. We can discuss a practical contact if you feel unsafe at home.
gi-diarrhea-dehydration: Oral rehydration solution has a particular balance of salts and sugar; a sports drink is not an identical substitute. I can show you the recommended product instructions and ask you to explain how you will take small amounts at home.
gi-epigastric-back-pain: We can discuss alcohol privately and without judgment. I ask because it can affect the safest evaluation and care; you do not need to discuss it in front of other patients or family members.
gi-progressive-dysphagia: Please tell the specialist about your fear of pain. They can explain comfort measures, the procedure and your choices before you consent. Let us address the concern so the swallowing and weight loss evaluation is not simply missed.
gi-right-lower-pain: We can speak privately without your partner present. I will ask permission before discussing sensitive information with anyone else. The pregnancy questions help us choose safe tests and consider urgent causes of pain.
gi-right-upper-pain: Ultrasound uses sound waves, not ionizing radiation. The team can explain the scan before it begins. What would you like clarified about the proposed evaluation?
neuro-acute-focal-weakness: Take your time; I can use one short question at a time and let you point or answer yes or no. I will not assume that difficulty finding words means you do not understand. We are arranging urgent help while we communicate.
neuro-back-bladder-redflags: Some nerves involved in bladder control travel through the lower back. Your new bladder and leg symptoms are why I recommend urgent assessment; this explanation is a concern to investigate, not a confirmed diagnosis.
neuro-distal-neuropathy: We can use a mirror or ask someone you trust to help inspect the soles of your feet. I will ask you to show or explain the method before you leave; if you notice a wound, arrange prompt assessment.
neuro-positional-vertigo: I understand that lying back can feel frightening. I will explain the position first, support you and stop if it is unsafe or you ask me to. You can choose whether to proceed after discussing it with the supervising clinician.
neuro-recurrent-headache: Let us choose one realistic change around studying, such as a regular meal or a protected sleep period, rather than trying to change everything at once. We can track the pattern and discuss what is workable at follow-up.
renal-acute-retention: We can keep this conversation private and discuss who, if anyone, you want involved. Embarrassment is understandable, but it should not delay relieving the retention and checking its cause.
renal-colicky-flank: Tell the care team that time away from work affects your income. We can discuss a practical follow-up arrangement and written instructions; fever, inability to drink or worsening illness still need urgent reassessment.
renal-dysuria: If an antibiotic is prescribed, follow its exact schedule and duration rather than stopping because burning improves. Contact the prescribing team about side effects or uncertainty. Please explain the schedule back once it has been prescribed.
renal-luts-nocturia: Please tell the prescribing clinician about your tendency to become lightheaded before starting any medicine. The plan should consider fall risk and your preferences; bladder symptoms alone do not require us to assume a particular drug is right for you.
renal-painless-hematuria: Let us arrange the evaluation before travel rather than waiting without a plan. Even blood that stops needs an explanation. We should identify whom to contact if bleeding returns or you cannot pass urine while away.
